deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 43% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 36% last year; 31%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: Not meaningful (the company holds more cash than its debt plus equity, or data is missing); return on shareholders' equity -16% (3 years ago -29%). (Tax rate estimated at 21%: effective rate not reported.)

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $2.9B, up 34% from a year ago — about 1.1× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $916M, up 42% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Stock-based pay is 21% of sales — a real cost to shareholders that cash-flow figures leave out.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 31%/yr over 3 years and 36%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today -14% vs a 5-year range of -21–-9% (median -14%): in the middle of its range.
deeper.margin_position: in the middle of its range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: No buybacks or dividends reported over the last 12 months. Share count up 2.2% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $1.83, up 9% in 90 days (up 9% in the last 30); 2 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $1.35, up 8% in 90 days (up 7% in the last 30); 1 analyst raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By region, latest quarter vs a year earlier: US 52% of sales, up 44%; Europe, Middle East, and Africa 26% of sales, up 32%; Asia Pacific 14% of sales, up 32%; Other 8% of sales, up 46%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +41% vs a year ago · $-0.67 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 41%, in step with sales (39%): growth comes from more business, not cost cuts.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 6 quarters running by about 7%: beating is now expected, so a small beat may not lift the stock.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 39% from a year ago and speeding up (from 34% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Operating margin -14%: it spends more to run the business than it earns from sales.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It kept $359M of cash after investment over 12 months.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: P/E isn't meaningful: earnings over the last 12 months were negative or missing.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share: how many years of today's profit you pay for.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 9% in 90 days (2 raised, 1 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
